pages.text: Ranger's plea after deer killed in dog attack at Bradgate Park Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Ranger's plea after deer killed in dog attack 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Ben Carr , East Midlands and Ben Jackson , BBC Radio Leicester NurPhoto via Getty Images Owners have been urged to keep their dogs under control after the deer's death (stock photo) A ranger has issued an appeal after a deer was killed by a dog at Bradgate Park. Matt Smith, head ranger at the park, said a previously "healthy deer" was found with its "underneath ripped out" close to the road running through the park on Monday morning. Bradgate Park Trust said in a statement it was a "heartbreaking reminder of the importance of keeping dogs under control". The death of the male fallow deer has not been reported to the police, the trust added. Smith said the incident had been "upsetting" for staff. "We've found what for all intents and purposes would have been quite a healthy deer dead at the side of the carriageway towards the Newtown Linford end, with all its sort of underneath ripped out," he added. "We're feeding a deer through the winter, keeping an eye on out for their wellbeing. Something as stupid as someone not having their dog on a lead, resulting in the death of one, is quite upsetting to all the staff and I should certainly think to members of the public as well. Among the Maya, smoking tobacco was more common than liquid consumption, shown by this smoking figure painted on a Maya vessel from the seventh or eighth century in Tikal, Guatemala. Album By Anna Thorpe Published September 19, 2024 Unprecedented archaeological evidence that the Maya used tobacco infusions for rituals related to sacrifice, bathing, and childbirth has been uncovered in the Pacific lowlands of Guatemala. Scientists working on the pre-Columbian archaeological site of El Baúl at Cotzumalhuapa were looking for traces of cacao in a sample of large ceramic vessels recovered from ritual deposits. Raw Flour and Dough Nov. 24, 2025 Español At a glance Uncooked flour and raw eggs can contain germs that can make you sick. Tasting or eating raw (unbaked) dough or batter can put you at risk for food poisoning. Follow the recipe or package directions for cooking or baking. Wash your hands, bowls, utensils, and countertops after handling raw flour, eggs, or dough. Risks of raw dough Most flour is raw Flour doesn't look like a raw food, but most flour is raw. That means it hasn't been treated to kill germs that cause food poisoning, such as Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Salmonella . These harmful germs can contaminate grain while it's still in the field or flour while it's being made. Steps like grinding grain and bleaching flour don't kill harmful germs—and these germs can end up in flour or baking mixes you buy at the store. You can get sick if you eat unbaked dough or batter made with flour containing germs. Germs are killed only when flour is baked or cooked. "The physics of the CMB is deep. Try sand sailing in Belgium Anyone can learn to sand yacht, all you need is a decent gust — and a good set of waterproofs. Sand yachting is one sport anyone can get good at quickly — unlike surfing, kitesurfing, windsurfing and many others. Westtoer By Colin Nicholson Published July 5, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). The wind catches my sail and the buggy trundles forward, reluctantly at first, before picking up speed. The crackle of old clam shells under my wheels grows increasingly insistent as I hurtle along, my head centimetres above the beach. Belgium’s coast may not be long, but it’s made up of one fine, wide, nearly unbroken stretch of sand, as I spotted yesterday on a walk from Westerpunt through the dunes, with their cuckoo calls and maze of caterpillar webs. It was from this vantage point that I saw sand yachts being launched on to De Panne beach like spaceships, the sleek, three-wheeled craft speeding off along the wet sand. I stood transfixed — suddenly, what had been a pleasant walk felt too pedestrian. As the tide starts coming in, it’s fun to speed over the shallows at the water’s edge and skirt the waves. Westtoer Luckily, sand yachting is one sport anyone can get good at quickly — unlike surfing, kitesurfing, windsurfing and many others. pages.text: Real Madrid: Man convicted for racist abuse of Kylian Mbappe - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Mbappe joined Real Madrid from Paris St-Germain in 2024 By Elizabeth Conway Spanish football reporter Published 17 November 2026 A man has been convicted of a hate crime after directing racist insults at Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe during a La Liga match at Real Oviedo in 2025. A court in Asturias, the northern Spanish region where Oviedo is based, handed down a guilty verdict against the man for the abuse at the Carlos Tartiere Stadium. The defendant was sentenced to 11 months in prison, alongside a fine and a number of additional disqualifications. The prison sentence has been suspended on the condition that he does not enter any stadium hosting official sporting competitions for a period of two years. The ruling represents another legal development in Spanish football's ongoing battle against racism, with Real Madrid continuing to pursue criminal action against individuals responsible for discriminatory abuse directed at the club's players. The club highlighted the latest conviction follows previous successful legal cases involving racist insults aimed at Vinicius Jr at Valencia's Mestalla , Mallorca's Son Moix, Rayo Vallecano's Vallecas and Real Valladolid's Jose Zorrilla stadiums. Real Madrid acted as a private prosecutor in the Asturias case and says the club will continue to take legal action in other incidents involving racist behaviour. Vaccinating children on time protects them and anyone around them with a weakened immune system. 1. Ideal timing The immunization schedule is carefully designed to provide protection at just the right time. Like all good babyproofing plans, CDC's recommended immunization schedule is safe and effective at protecting your baby. It's based on how your child's immune system responds to vaccines at various ages, and how likely your baby is to be exposed to a particular disease. This ensures your little one is protected from 14 potentially serious diseases at exactly the right time. On the other hand, there is no data to support that spacing out vaccines offers safe or effective protection from these diseases. July 3, 2024 Reasons to Get Vaccinated Key points All children ages 11–12-years should get HPV vaccine to protect against cancers caused by HPV infections. Why it's important Almost every unvaccinated perso n who is sexually active will get HPV at some time in their life. About 13 million Americans, including teens, become infected with HPV each year. Most HPV infections will go away on their own. But infections that don’t go away can cause certain types of cancer. HPV can cause cancers of the: Cervix, vagina, and vulva in women Penis in men Anus in both women and men Back of the throat (called oropharyngeal cancer), including the base of the tongue and tonsils, in both men and women What the data show HPV vaccination works. HPV infections, genital warts, and cervical pre-cancers (abnormal cells on the cervix that can lead to cancer) have dropped since the vaccine has been in use in the United States. Infections with HPV types that cause most HPV cancers and genital warts have dropped 88% among teen girls and 81% among young adult women. pages.text: Reconstructing the Bocksten Man’s face | National Geographic Premium HISTORY MAGAZINE Reconstructing the face of a 700-year-old murder victim Now known as Bocksten Man, his body was stashed at the bottom of the bog by his killer attempting to hide the crime. Unbeknownst to them, the water’s natural chemistry slows the decay of human remains. Living image Oscar Nilsson’s recreation of Bocksten Man relied on the mortal remains as well as the garments found with the body. Charlotta Sandelin/Halland Museum of Cultural History By Amy Briggs Published August 17, 2023 • 5 min read The day before Midsummer’s Eve in June 1936, five-year-old Gulli Johanssen tagged along with her older brother Thure as he went to harvest peat in Bocksten Bog in Varberg, Sweden. The Johansson children were shocked to discover bones in the ground and summoned their father, Albert. He notified the police, who then summoned local experts, including Albert Sandklef, director of the Varberg Museum. Together they determined the body was not a recent victim of foul play; it had been there for centuries. They could see that much of the bones still lay below the earth, but pieces of cloth and wooden stakes were visible above ground. The body and clothing were carefully excavated from the site and taken to the museum where they were preserved and studied. ( These mummies were made … by accident? ) Real readhead? Bocksten Man's hair color in life was blonder, but the acidic bog waters turned it much tawnier over time. Smithsonian Enterprises -- along with other media companies, paper companies and catalogers -- is a supporter of Recycling Works in Publishing (RWIP). RWIP is a member of The Recycling Partnership , a program of Curbside Value Partnership, whose goal is to increase curbside recycling in communities throughout the U.S. The Recycling Partnership (recyclingpartnership.org) is a national nonprofit, transforming recycling in towns all across America. They believe that recycling is fundamental to a healthy environment and economy. Every day, they work hand-in-hand with communities and companies, continuously innovating to improve recycling systems. The Recycling Partnership works at the community-level to provide free tools, assistance and grants to improve the quality and quantity of curbside recycling. Recovering more bottles, cans, containers and paper means less carbon emissions, more water savings, more energy savings, and a new supply of feedstock for manufacturing. The Recycling Partnership also works across the entire recycling system to drive collaboration and innovation. They make connections, solve problems, open dialogs, and partner to set the pace for a brighter, more sustainable future. Want to hear more? Visit recyclingpartnership.org . pages.text: REDs: how relative energy deficiency in sport affects athletes - BBC Sport By Sarah Dawkins BBC Sport senior journalist Warning: this article contains discussion of eating disorders "If you keep this up, you'll be in a wheelchair at 30." That is what doctors told British long-distance runner Jake Smith four years ago. From the outside looking in, his career was flying. By the age of 23, he had signed a professional contract with Nike and represented Great Britain on the global stage. But at the same time, his body was deteriorating - enduring a relentless pattern of race, illness, injury, repeat. Balancing an intense training regime with disordered eating meant the 28-year-old returned from a running camp in Uganda weighing just eight stone (51kg) at 5ft 5in (1.7m). He had such brittle bones that he was told his career could be over. After suffering two stress fractures in the space of four months, Smith sought professional help and was diagnosed with REDs – relative energy deficiency in sport. It is a syndrome that can affect anyone and if left undiagnosed or untreated, can have an impact on performance and cause serious, long-lasting health problems. The symptoms are slightly better documented in women - just last month, tennis player Emma Navarro revealed her diagnosis and subsequent decision to step away from competition until 2027. But men are just as susceptible and due to stigma and lack of obvious warning signs, it can go undetected for longer and means many, like Smith, suffer in silence. pages.text: Reference Files Reference Files Skip Navigation Within Census Geographies Reference Files Geographic Reference Files are documents that list codes for geographic entities. These include Relationship Files, Gazetteer Files, Block Assignment Files, and Tally Files. Relationship Files describe geographic relationships over time and between types. Geographic Relationships Over Time show the relationships (comparability) for the same type of geography over different periods of time (e.g. the relationship between places in 2010 and 2000). Geographic Relationships Between Entity Types show the relationship between different types of geography for the same period (e.g. the relationships between congressional districts and places). Gazetteer Files list geographic entities, such as county, place, and census tracts, with information on name, geographic code, population, housing unit counts, and latitude/longitude of the internal point. Credit: AdobeStock Regenerative medicine therapy, including cell therapy, gene therapy, and therapeutic tissue engineering, provides unprecedented potential to treat, modify, reverse, or cure previously intractable diseases, such as cancer and organ failures. This class of therapy has completely changed the paradigm and the trajectory for medical treatment.
